Audio & Voice Settings

General Audio Configuration
Allow voice input via microphone. Requires whisper-cli or compatible ASR engine.
Status: checking...
Allow AI responses to be spoken aloud. Requires Piper or MeloTTS backend.
Status: checking...
Automatically speak every AI response when it completes.
Hold the mic button to record instead of toggling on/off.
Master volume for all text-to-speech playback (0 = mute).
Speech Recognition (ASR) Engine
Select the speech recognition backend. Auto picks based on available hardware.
Large models require 8+ GB VRAM or 16+ GB RAM.
Language for transcription. Auto attempts to detect from audio.
Hardware to run ASR inference on. CUDA requires NVIDIA GPU.
Parallel computation threads for CPU inference. Higher = faster but more CPU usage.
Number of beams for beam-search decoding. Higher = more accurate but slower.
Number of candidate transcriptions to evaluate. Higher = better accuracy.
Sampling randomness. 0 = deterministic, 1 = maximum randomness. Lower is more accurate.
Automatically translate all recognized speech to English before sending.
Remove timestamps from output. Cleaner text but loses timing info.
Enable Flash Attention for faster inference on modern GPUs. Disable if encountering errors.
Text-to-Speech (TTS) Engine
Select the speech synthesis backend. Piper and Kokoro run locally. MeloTTS requires remote server.
MeloTTS requires HOWL_MELOTTS_URL environment variable. Kokoro requires Python + kokoro package.
Piper .onnx voice models. Add a directory once — HOWL remembers it and picks up new voices automatically on startup.
Playback speed multiplier. 1.0 = normal, 0.5 = half speed, 2.0 = double speed.
Piper-specific: randomness in audio generation. 0.667 = default. Lower = cleaner, more robotic.
Piper-specific: phoneme width noise. 0.8 = default. Affects naturalness of speech.
Seconds of silence added after each sentence. 0.2 = default pause between sentences.
Cache synthesized audio to disk to avoid re-generating identical phrases.
Maximum disk space for TTS cache in megabytes. Oldest files are removed first.
MB
Voice Activity Detection
Voice Activity Detection automatically splits speech and removes silence. Recommended for ASR.
VAD requires a compatible model. May increase latency slightly.
Confidence level (0-1) required to classify audio as speech. Higher = fewer false positives.
Minimum milliseconds of speech required before a segment is kept. Filters out short noises.
ms
Milliseconds of silence required to split speech into separate segments.
ms
Milliseconds of padding added before and after detected speech segments.
ms
Audio Hardware & I/O
Microphone or audio input source for speech recognition.
Speaker or audio output device for TTS playback.
Audio sample rate for recording and playback. 16 kHz is optimal for ASR. 44.1 kHz is CD quality.
Mono is required for ASR. Stereo is supported for playback.
Audio bit depth for recording. 16-bit is standard. 24/32-bit offers higher dynamic range.
Input gain for microphone recording. Increase if speech is too quiet, decrease if clipping.
Settings persist automatically across sessions
